# Results — Study 720 (Super-Bowl-Advertiser)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore — a company that buys
a **Super Bowl commercial** gets a burst of attention and its stock **drifts up in the days
after the game** (the "big-ad signal"), with a real 2005 finance paper behind it — tested as a
small **event study** over a hardcoded, transparent table of ~32 real listed Super Bowl
advertisers (advertiser-years, 2015–2024). Around each game we measure the abnormal
(excess-of-SPY) return on a short **drift** leg `[+1…+5d]` after the Monday and a longer **hold**
leg `[+6…+25d]`, plus the single-day **Monday reaction** `[0,0]`, with a 1-day entry lag. Offline
& deterministic for the synthetic control; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — SPY + ~26 advertiser tickers (public, no key) |
| As-of (cache) | **2026-07-10** (window 2013-06-03 → 2026-07-10; event windows fall within it) |
| Advertiser table | **32** documented listed advertiser-years; **11** famous ones DELISTED / taken private (named) |
| Table fingerprint | `fc267dcab645` (sha1 of ticker@game-date pairs, first 12 hex) |
| Events priced | **32** of 32 (all in-window; SQSP dropped — taken private Oct 2024 — replaced pre-registration) |
| Legs | abnormal excess-of-SPY return over `[0,0]` (Monday), `[+1…+5d]` (drift), `[+6…+25d]` (hold) |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag (act Monday close, drift starts Tuesday); large-cap one-way 10 bps × 2 crossings |

> **Survivorship caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The loudest Super Bowl advertisers in
> history — **Pets.com** (the sock puppet, SB 2000), **Computer.com**, **Kozmo.com**,
> **LifeMinders.com**, the dot-com class of 2000, **Just for Feet** (SB 1999) — **went bust** and
> leave **no** yfinance series; **Squarespace** (a Super Bowl regular) was **taken private** by
> Permira (Oct 2024) and also left the public tape. The priced sample is therefore the set of
> advertisers that *survived and stayed listed*, biased **toward** names that did not collapse and
> **for** the believers' "advertising pays" claim. A survivor-only drift near zero is thus a
> **conservative** refutation.

## The signal — abnormal returns on each leg vs zero

1-day entry lag. The Welch *t* tests each leg's cross-sectional mean against zero; the placebo *p*
is the share of 20,000 random same-size non-event windows (same tickers) whose mean abnormal
return matches/beats the advertiser set in magnitude.

| leg | n | mean abnormal | win-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Monday reaction** `[0,0]`  | 32 | **−0.33%** | 41% | **−0.83** | — |
| **drift** `[+1…+5d]`         | 32 | **+0.39%** | 47% | **+0.31** | 0.637 |
| **hold** `[+6…+25d]`         | 32 | **+1.20%** | 50% | **+0.60** | 0.471 |

Read it carefully. The **drift** — the believers' "big-ad signal" — is a faint **+0.4%** abnormal
return over the first week, on a **47%** win-rate (*below* a coin flip) and **t = 0.31**:
indistinguishable from no drift at all, and dead-center in the placebo cloud (*p* = 0.64). The
**Monday reaction** is actually **negative** (−0.33%, t = −0.83) — the ad airs, the world watches,
and the stock, if anything, dips. The **hold** leg is a shrug (+1.2%, t = 0.60). The one-legged
story needs a significant **+drift**; the tape delivers an insignificant whisper on a sub-50%
win-rate. The signal isn't there.

## By era — the drift flips sign, a hallmark of noise

| era | n | mean drift | mean hold |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2015–17 | 3 | +2.79% | +6.66% |
| 2019–21 | 12 | **−1.32%** | +3.66% |
| 2022–24 | 17 | +1.17% | −1.49% |

The drift is positive early, **negative** in 2019–21, and flat recently — it wanders with the
sample rather than persisting. No era shows a stable "advertising pays" drift.

## The ad-calendar basket earns a rounding error

The folklore trade is: **buy every advertiser Monday, sell a week later** (the drift leg).

| | per-event P&L |
|---|--:|
| gross drift `[+1…+5d]` | **+0.39%** |
| net @ 10 bps × 2 crossings | **+0.19%** |
| gross hold-through `[+1…+25d]` | +1.59% |
| net @ 10 bps × 2 crossings | +1.39% |

The five-day basket is **+0.39% gross / +0.19% net** — a rounding error inside its own standard
error, on a sub-50% win-rate, indistinguishable from a week of February large-cap beta. There is
nothing to harvest.

## Robustness — the result is flat in the window choice

| drift / hold days | n | drift mean | drift *t* | hold mean | hold *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 / 10   | 32 | +0.76% | +0.93 | −0.31% | −0.20 |
| **5 / 20** | 32 | +0.39% | +0.31 | +1.20% | +0.60 |
| 10 / 40  | 32 | +1.71% | +1.13 | −2.92% | −1.02 |

No window makes the drift significant (no *t* clears 1.2), and the hold leg flips sign across
horizons. The verdict does not hinge on the exact window.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and ~32 events are weak

On deterministic event windows where we *plant* a known post-game drift of size `edge` (seed 726):

| planted edge | n | drift mean | drift *t* | hold mean | hold *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 32 | −0.03% | −0.05 | +0.20% | +0.09 |
| **+0.10** (10% drift) | 32 | +10.48% | +13.23 | +0.20% | +0.09 |

With **no** planted edge the drift *t* is ~0 (it cannot manufacture significance from ~32 noisy
events); only a **+10%** planted drift lights up the drift leg (*t* = 13.2). The control proves the
measurement engine is unbiased **and** that a few-dozen events can only detect an implausibly large
effect — exactly why a survivor table of ~32 advertisers cannot certify the legend.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The drift is **+0.4%** at **t = 0.31** (placebo *p* = 0.64) on a *sub-50%*
  win-rate, and the day-one reaction is **negative** (−0.33%, t = −0.83). Fehle, Tsyplakov &
  Zdorovtsov (2005) found the effect on a 2000–04 sample, but this modern tape is indistinguishable
  from noise ⇒ **NONE**, not WEAK. Survivorship is named on this axis: the advertisers that went
  bust delisted, biasing the surviving drift *up*.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-the-advertisers basket is **+0.39% gross / +0.19% net** over
  five days — a rounding error inside its own SE, indistinguishable from a week of February beta.
  There is no edge to harvest, at any size.
- **Big-ad signal? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The legend is a much-cited 2005 result plus a memorable sock
  puppet (Pets.com, remembered *because* it was extreme, and **delisted**). Across a representative
  modern survivor table the post-game drift is a coin-flip and the day-one move is negative. Real as
  a 2005 paper, absent as a modern edge.
